summary:
MARS CODE is an educational 3D simulator that transforms the abstract concepts of space mission design into an interactive learning experience. While many simulators focus solely on the spacecraft construction phase, we designed a solution that allows students to experience the complexities of Surface Operations.

Participants take on the role of a JPL Rover Planner, making critical engineering decisions by programming an autonomous rover using visual code blocks (Scratch-style). To succeed, players must navigate orbital constraints and manage limited resources—such as power (battery), mass limits, and data communications—while completing scientific objectives.

The simulation's logic and constraints are driven by real NASA data and frameworks, specifically integrating the Concept Maturity Level (CML) and Mission Design Lab (MDL) trade rules into our core architecture (CML_Progression.json and MDL_TradeRules.json). By evaluating how each block of code shapes the success or failure of the mission telemetry, MARS CODE bridges the gap between mission concept and active operation, making space engineering accessible and engaging for the next generation.
details:
MARS CODE is an interactive educational game that teaches programming fundamentals through missions for the ROVER-01 Mars rover. Players choose a mission, connect visual command blocks in a Scratch-inspired editor, and run a simulation to see the rover follow their program. The game introduces sequences, loops, conditions, variables, and sensors through challenges that gradually become more complex.

The project builds algorithmic thinking through hands-on experimentation and problem-solving, without requiring a physical rover or special equipment. Players can complete missions, track their progress, and save their algorithms. The interface is available in both Ukrainian and English.

MARS CODE is a browser-based application built with React, TypeScript, Blockly, and React Three Fiber. Progress and programs are saved locally in the browser. The project combines Scratch’s approachable visual programming with Mars missions and rover simulation to make learning programming clear, practical, and engaging.
